prompt:
Below is part of a flattened Claude Code session transcript. Each line is `L<n><TAB>role<TAB>kind<TAB>text`, where role is user or assistant and kind is text, tool_use, tool_result or tool_error. Find moments of friction between the user and Claude, of four kinds:
- correction: the user corrects or redirects Claude (says it was wrong, to stop, to do something else, or repeats an instruction Claude missed). An answer to a question Claude asked (a tool_result like "The user answered: ..." or picking an option) is NOT a correction unless it rejects what Claude proposed.
- stuck: Claude retries the same thing, loops, or says it is stuck.
- tool_error: a tool result reports an error that changed Claude's course.
- permission_denial: a tool call was denied or blocked by a permission rule or the user.
Rules: cite the line id (for example L123) of the line that shows the friction. The quote must be copied verbatim, character for character, from that cited line only, at most 200 characters. Emit no row when you are not sure. Emit at most 15 rows. Return an empty rows array if there is no friction in this text. The note is a short plain description, at most 120 characters.
